reasoning.Student D:
Since the mechanism guarantees that my Obtainable Schools set is fixed regardless of how I rank schools, my ranking only determines which school I receive *within* that set—specifically, my most preferred school among those obtainable to me. This is the defining property of a strategy-proof mechanism (like the Deferred Acceptance algorithm), where truthful reporting is a dominant strategy.

Given this, there is no strategic benefit to misrepresenting my preferences. If I rank a less-preferred school higher, I risk receiving it instead of a more-preferred school that was actually obtainable to me. Conversely, ranking a school I prefer more highly cannot hurt me, since the obtainable set doesn't change based on my ranking—only my selection within that set does.

Therefore, the optimal strategy is to submit my true preference ordering: w > y > x > z. This ensures that whatever schools are obtainable to me, I will be matched to the one I most prefer among them.

I should ignore the information about other applicants' aggregate preferences (y > x > w > z) and my priority ranks, since these do not change the strategic advice: truth-telling is always optimal in this mechanism.
